Q: Copy all registry entries from one location to the other in Inno Setup A:

There's no easy way to copy registry tree elsewhere.

  • You can use WinAPI RegCopyTree (but you will also need to import and use RegOpenKey, RegCreateKey and RegCloseKey).

  • If you want to stick with plain Pascal Script, you would have to use RegGetSubkeyNames and RegGetValueNames to collect all subkeys and values and copy/write them one-by-one.

    For some example, see Copy32BitUninstallKeyTo64bit in Keep existing 32-bit Inno Setup installation path for upgrades, use 64-bit path for new installations – though it does copy only all values (and of specific types only), not subkeys.

Q: Flutter SSL Handshake Failure on Android 13 and below A:

Thanks for the suggestion.

Yes, on the Android 13 and below devices that we tested, DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 does not appear to be present in the system CA store, while on Android 14+ the connection works without any modification.

Because of this, the TLS handshake fails with:

CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED: self signed certificate in certificate chain

As a workaround, we added the DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 certificate to a custom SecurityContext in Flutter while keeping the system trusted roots enabled:

final context = SecurityContext(withTrustedRoots: true);
context.setTrustedCertificatesBytes(certData.buffer.asUint8List());

This resolved the issue on Android 13 and below devices without disabling SSL verification or bypassing certificate validation.

My main concern is whether adding the required root CA to the Flutter SecurityContext like this is considered an acceptable and secure approach for production apps distributed through Google Play, or if there is a more recommended way to handle such CA compatibility issues in Flutter for older Android versions.

Q: Is it undefined behavior to store any value other than zero or one in a `bool` in C++? A:

Addendum: bool gives you guarantees on what you can put into them without playing tricks on the compiler. This lets the compiler pick off bugs for you. If you have to play tricks, bool probably isn't the right choice. Use the appropriate integer type or, if the gods smile upon you, an enum class so you can still get the compiler doing sanity checks for you.
